newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends steady vs dlr, forwards inch up.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends steady vs dlr, forwards inch up.

text.p: The Indian rupee ended steady against the dollar on Thursday after slipping initially on a spurt in demand for dollars, dealers said.
In two-way movement, the rupee which opened Thursday at 35.73/75 per dollar touched a low of 35.76 before recovering to close at 35.73/75, they said.
"There was some dollar demand from some local banks and from an east-India based bank," a dealer said. "Some banks may have been short," he said.
The combined demand pushed the rupee down before dollar selling by other banks helped it recover, he said. "Supplies remain good," he said.
In the forward market, premia firmed up marginally on expectations of higher call money rates, dealers said.
The premia for six-month dollars ended Thursday at 10.92 percent annualised against Wednesday's 10.64 percent.
